Explain the difference between the natural greenhouse effect and the enhanced greenhouse effect.
Greenhouse gases (CO₂, H₂O, CH₄) are naturally present
These gases trap heat from the Sun
Keeps Earth at about 15°C (without it would be -18°C)

Burning fossil fuels adds extra CO₂
More greenhouse gases trap more heat
Earth's temperature is rising above natural levels
Describe two sources of carbon dioxide and two sources of methane in the atmosphere.
- Coal, oil, and natural gas are burned for energy in power stations, transport, and heating. This releases CO₂ that was locked away for millions of years.
- Trees absorb CO₂ by photosynthesis. When forests are burned or cut down, this CO₂ is released and less is absorbed.
- Cattle and sheep produce methane during digestion. Rice paddies also produce methane from waterlogged soil.
- Organic waste in landfills decomposes without oxygen (anaerobic conditions), producing methane gas.
Describe three pieces of evidence that climate change is occurring.
Global average temperature has increased by about 1.1°C since 1850

Ice cores show this is unusual compared to thousands of years of history
Sea levels are rising at about 3.7 mm per year
This is caused by thermal expansion of water and melting ice
Coastal areas are experiencing increased flooding
